title: Bilinear Fourier integral transposition for integrable functions
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field] and Lebesgue measures. Let $a,b\geq1$, let $L:\mathbf R^a\times\mathbf R^b\to\mathbf R$ be continuous and real bilinear, and let $f:\mathbf R^a\to\mathbf C$ and $q:\mathbf R^b\to\mathbf C$ be measurable with $\int|f|<\infty$ and $\int|q|<\infty$. Define $J_Lf(y)=\int e^{-2\pi i L(\xi,y)}f(\xi)\,d\xi$ and $J_{L^{\mathrm t}}q(\xi)=\int e^{-2\pi i L(\xi,y)}q(y)\,dy$. Then $$\int J_Lf(y)q(y)\,dy=\int f(\xi)J_{L^{\mathrm t}}q(\xi)\,d\xi.$$ The notation $L^{\mathrm t}(y,\xi)=L(\xi,y)$ denotes the transposed bilinear form.
